name: Labor Zionism
summary: Labor Zionism joins Jewish national revival in Palestine with a socialist or labour-centred programme: a Jewish commonwealth built by Jewish workers on national land, with co-operative and collective settlement, trade unions and the revival of Hebrew. Its strands differ on class struggle and Marxism (Borochov and Syrkin against Hapoel Hatzair and Katznelson's constructivism), and Ben-Gurion's Mapai added a democratic, law-based state with a mixed economy.
scope: Mainstream Labor Zionism c. 1905-1968: Borochov's Poale Zion, Syrkin's Socialist Zionism, A. D. Gordon's Hapoel Hatzair, and Ahdut HaAvoda, Mapai and the Histadrut, as stated in Borochov, Syrkin, Katznelson, Ben-Gurion and the Poale Zion programmes. It excludes Revisionism, religious Zionism, Hashomer Hatzair and Mapam, the later Israeli Labor Party, the State of Israel's actions as such, and socialism in general; statements those sources do not settle are null.

sources.title: Labor Zionism
sources.author: Donna Robinson Divine, Encyclopedia of the Modern Middle East and North Africa (via encyclopedia.com)
sources.usedFor: Strands: Hapoel Hatzair (no class struggle, no strikes), Poale Zion, Histadrut, kibbutz and moshav, Mapai.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Ben-Gurion holds that "so long as wars are possible, without an Army our security" cannot be assured, and Poale Zion's Hashomer and self-defence are part of its record.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Katznelson says "those who speak about a strong arm are just playing with strong words" and that violence is no solution, defending constructive work over armed adventure.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Poale Zion calls compulsory assimilation of Jews in other states "anything but a virtue", yet Ben-Gurion wants Jewish immigrants to Israel educated and "assimilated" into one Hebrew nation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Ben-Gurion says democracy "would be suicidal" if it allowed only its enemies to act "and condemn itself to impotence by divesting itself of all means of defense", and warns against parties that seek one-party rule.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Syrkin says imperialism, colonial policy and militarism were "the life-giving diet" of the capitalist powers and traces the World War to them; Borochov calls international competition "a consequence of capitalist economy".

central-planning.rationale: Syrkin wants the Jewish state built on "social planning", while Ben-Gurion says "We are not wedded to total planning, believers in a wholly regimented economy" yet wants "some broad pattern of employment, housing, and the husbandry"; the strands differ.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Syrkin calls "the sacredness of nations, their absolute right to life, growth and equality" the content of internationalism and attacks the "imperialism" of ruling nations.

class-collaboration.rationale: Katznelson defends "class collaboration in Zionism" for building a homeland of labor, whereas Borochov's Social Democratic Poale Zion wants Zionism "without renouncing the class struggle against the bourgeoisie for even a minute".

class-struggle-history.rationale: Syrkin writes "Class struggle is the main driving force of history" and Borochov builds on Marx, but Hapoel Hatzair rejected class struggle as a tool and most socialist doctrine, and Katznelson ranks national construction above "pure class struggle".

clerical-rule.rationale: Ben-Gurion says the state will not be a theocracy, as Mizrahi and Agudah once declared, and denies that the rabbis of Agudah are "exclusively the repository of power in Israel to make laws".

collective-farming.rationale: Hapoel Hatzair founded both the first kibbutz and the first moshav, and Ben-Gurion praises the kvutza while stressing private farmers too; the movement accepted both collective and co-operative family farming.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Poale Zion wants development of backward lands "not for the sake of exploitation for a mother country", and Syrkin calls imperialism and colonial policies the diet of ruling nations.

conscription.rationale: Ben-Gurion plans "Two years' conscription" for the Israeli army, supplemented by longer regular service.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ben-Gurion says "Where the people is not free to make its laws, through representatives of its own free choice, not the law rules--but arbitrary dictatorship", and that government must be "chosen by the people in free ballot".

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Ben-Gurion says "The people, as legislator, must not be circumscribed" and that the judge "neither makes the law nor unmakes it"; he still insists on rule of law and free minorities, so this is a moderate agreement.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Katznelson calls the "superior culture and language of the ruling nation" argument "snobbish" and Syrkin says humanity "would be impoverished spiritually" if national characteristics disappeared.

democracy-best.rationale: Ben-Gurion told the Knesset "Democracy's destiny is ours" and that "the rule of law is inconceivable without the rule of democracy"; he trusts a free people to "correct its mistakes".

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Ben-Gurion holds that "The crux is the Right of Return of Jewry dispersed, a prerogative of rebuilding and development, of freedom and sovereignty".

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Katznelson denounces seizure of power by violence, saying such revolutions in South America changed governments without helping the masses, and warns the labour movement not to adopt fascist methods; Ben-Gurion calls the Soviet system "a Communist dictatorship".

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ben-Gurion holds that "By passing laws for itself, in the light of its own will and wants, the people affirms its sovereignty", against the view that only Holy Writ has sovereign force.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Ben-Gurion holds that for Israel "it is a charter of duties that is needed ... what we owe to Homeland and nation", yet Syrkin and Katznelson insist no person is a means to the community's ends.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Ben-Gurion approves that "under certain conditions" it is "necessary to withdraw his freedom from a man who endangers" rule of law and democracy, citing Britain's wartime detention of an MP.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Syrkin calls for an international league of nations as "a legal, political organ" that would administer canals and strategic points and make a code of law between nations, with "the elevation of humanity over the individual states".

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Ben-Gurion told the Knesset in 1950 that Israel does not need "an unbending and haughty Constitution, that fetters the Legislature" and rejected a charter "privileged and rigid" above ordinary law, preferring ordinary basic laws.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Katznelson says "Your blood is not more precious than mine", calling the opposite "the complete negation of socialist ethics", and Poale Zion demands equal rights for every national group.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Katznelson argues that "formal equality alone will never abolish poverty" and that where it fails the oppressed "it is our right, nay, our duty, to deviate from the niceties of formal equality for the sake of real and living equality", though he speaks of protecting the underprivileged, not of equal outcomes.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Poale Zion aims to concentrate "a Jewish majority in Palestine", and Ben-Gurion wants Jews no longer "a minority", but both promise civil and national rights for non-Jews and reject domination of one group over another.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Ben-Gurion says "The rights to Palestine do not, as in those countries they do, belong to the existing settlers, whether it be Jews or Arabs"; the claim rests on the Return of dispersed Jewry, not on current residence.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Ben-Gurion states that "Six million Jews, men and women alike, babes in arms and the old and helpless, were done to death with calculated and systematic barbarity".

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The 1909 Poale Zion programme "aims to concentrate the Jewish people in Palestine", and Katznelson names "national reconcentration" as the task; Ben-Gurion holds the ingathering of the exiles to be the purpose of the state.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Gordon wrote "We come to our Homeland in order to be planted in our natural soil from which we have been uprooted"; labour, he said, "binds a people to its soil and to its national culture".

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Katznelson holds that "a homeland will not be constructed upon speculation and absentee landlordism" and demands "a homeland of labor"; Poale Zion protested the use of National Fund money to enrich real-estate speculators.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Poale Zion demands rights for the Jewish people as a group: "national equality in the general government and complete self-government in Jewish national affairs", and proportional national representation.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Every Poale Zion programme aims "to establish ... an autonomous Jewish commonwealth" in Palestine, the Confederation seeks "the territorial solution of the Jewish question", and Ben-Gurion builds the state.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Jewish National Fund buys land "that is to remain forever the property of the Jewish nation", described by Poale Zion as "a socialistic institution"; the sources do not say settlers hold it only while they use it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ben-Gurion answered the claim that "A Constitution made by human hands can have no place in Israel" by arguing that "the laws that men make for their own needs" are legitimate and that the people "affirms its sovereignty" by legislating.

leader-cult.rationale: Katznelson condemns the craving "to prostrate oneself before a fuehrer" and the "cult of authority and obedience borrowed from the army" as the base of fascism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Katznelson urges the youth movements to keep alive the memory of comrades who fell in self-defence at Hulda, Tel Chai and Homel, and of those who died for Jewish labour.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Borochov derives nationalism from "conditions of production" yet calls himself "a Marxist without matter", and Katznelson says the belief in inevitable historical forces has failed and "other forces" must count, so the strands differ.

means-match-ends.rationale: Katznelson holds "Between their methods and their goal there is an inner harmony. When we shall adopt their methods, we shall become like them" and rejects imitating Fascism to fight it.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Ben-Gurion holds that every citizen "soldier, official, Minister of State ... is subordinate to the law", and Katznelson condemns "the cult of authority and obedience borrowed from the army".

minority-language-support.rationale: Poale Zion demands "the right to receive an education in its own speech through self taxation or ... proportional refunding of taxes" and, in Turkey, "unabridged freedom of the language which each people recognizes as its own".

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Syrkin says "Nationalism means territorial autonomy--cultural autonomy is but a compromise with cold historical reality" and that autonomy "is no solution to the problem of the Jewish people"; Poale Zion still demands cultural autonomy in the Diaspora meanwhile.

national-self-determination.rationale: Syrkin holds "The sacredness of nations, their absolute right to life, growth and equality--this is internationalism", and "free nationalism must be proclaimed as holy and inviolate"; Poale Zion demands "the right of self-determination" for the Jews.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Syrkin says the Jewish masses "will not accept a capitalistic Jewish state" and Katznelson condemns "communistic Russia" and the imitation of Fascism, while Ben-Gurion calls the Soviet Union "a Communist dictatorship"; they look for a labour-based third course.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The Palestinian Poale Zion platform demands "secular school study in the national mother tongue".

one-party-rule.rationale: Ben-Gurion rejects "the absolute rule of a single party" and says of totalitarian regimes "We must avoid this like the plague"; Poale Zion calls democracy "one of the most significant weapons" of the working class.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Katznelson holds that "the protection and the construction of our homeland go hand in hand with the class struggle", calling it "a homeland of labor for all Israel".

people-in-arms.rationale: Ben-Gurion says two years' conscription "will not answer all the needs of Army and security" and calls for volunteers to serve "three to five years more", i.e. a standing cadre, though he also wants a citizen army.

person-over-state.rationale: Syrkin applies Kant's principle that "man was not a tool for use by other men" to society and nations; Katznelson says "The individual is not a means or a tool to be used by another".

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Katznelson calls for "the tender cultivation of all that is vital in Jewish tradition" and says a culture "isolated from our own soil" will not raise the needed generations; Poale Zion fights assimilation and fosters Jewish culture.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The 1918 Poale Zion outline says capitalist production and distribution "are based on the exploitation of the millions of workers of the world", but Hapoel Hatzair avoided socialist doctrine and no Mapai text states this.

property-fundamental.rationale: Poale Zion programmes aim at abolishing private ownership of the means of production, and the Jewish National Fund land is to "remain forever the property of the Jewish nation"; Ben-Gurion still leaves room for private capital, so the rejection is firm but not absolute.

public-ownership.rationale: The Poale Zion programmes aim at "the taking over by the people themselves of the means of production" (Palestine party, 1910) and "the socialization of the means of production" (Confederation); Ben-Gurion adds that "the State itself must take first heed for basic industries".

refugee-return.rationale: Ben-Gurion welcomes that for the Arab refugees "the only practical solution of the problem is their resettlement in the Arab countries" and notes that views advocating their return had lost ground.

religious-nation.rationale: Poale Zion treats the Jews as "one nation dispersed in various countries" and says the wealthy assimilationists "create the illusion that the Jews are merely a religious sect".

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The Palestinian Poale Zion platform (1910) demands "absolute freedom of unionization and the right to strike".

results-over-ideology.rationale: Katznelson says "We shall judge every suggested plan of action by whether it leads to strengthening the power of the worker ... and if not, then the devil with splendor, romanticism and tradition", and prefers "a living idea" to "mummified doctrines".

revive-national-language.rationale: The Palestinian Poale Zion platform "considers Hebrew as the national language of the Jews", furthers its spread and demands its official recognition; Katznelson lists "the rebirth of the Hebrew language" among the movement's tasks.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Poale Zion "accept only one radical solution for these injustices--Zionism", and Katznelson says "the genuine emancipation of the Jewish worker is unthinkable without the emancipation of the Jewish people from the Diaspora".

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Gordon holds that the Jewish people "has been completely cut off from nature and imprisoned within city walls" and needs labour that, he said, "binds a people to its soil"; Ben-Gurion praises the villages with "no shopkeepers or speculators".

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Katznelson says "Creative revolutionaries do not throw the cultural heritage of ages into the dust-bin" and calls the wish to destroy the old world entirely a sinister reaction.

separated-powers.rationale: Ben-Gurion says "the legislative power entrusted to the elected representatives of the people is totally sundered from the judicial", the judges being "independent of the Executive"; ministers and officials are bound by the law.

simple-living.rationale: Gordon wrote that "no man with a soul can be happy in the possession of luxuries"; no other strand states a position on simple living.

single-official-language.rationale: The Palestinian Poale Zion platform demands for every nationality "equality and the unabridged freedom of the language which each people recognizes as its own", while seeking official recognition of Hebrew without banning others.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The 1918 Poale Zion outline calls the existing state "primarily an instrument protecting the powers and rights of only one group--the ruling capitalistic class", but sees a socialist-national state differently.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Ben-Gurion holds that "in the interest of security the State itself must take first heed for basic industries ... with the aid of private capital or without it", while leaving other branches to private initiative.

state-harmful.rationale: Poale Zion and Syrkin seek a Jewish state, and Ben-Gurion calls the people's own laws an affirmation of sovereignty; only Borochov personally calls himself an "anarchist-socialist", and he leaves that a private view.

strong-leader.rationale: Katznelson rejects the "craving to obey" a leader in military uniform, and Ben-Gurion warns that governments not chosen by the people become an end "however praiseworthy in itself", citing dictatorships that claimed to serve public welfare.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Ben-Gurion holds that in a democracy the minority "may without constraint express opinions, think as it chooses, vote as it sees fit" and that Israel allows even an anti-Zionist party.

total-state.rationale: Ben-Gurion says "A totalitarian State will not recognize man's independent worth" and that totalitarian rule "spells ruin"; Katznelson attacks the "cult of authority and obedience" behind the fascist state.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Ben-Gurion says the totalitarian regimes, Fascist and Soviet, "have this in common: that none tolerates individual liberty or the rule of law, or free criticism", and Katznelson fears "species A and species B" of Fascism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ben-Gurion calls the Jews "an old race" with an unbroken memory of several thousand years, whereas Borochov holds that modern nations are products of capitalist production conditions.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Katznelson warns his youth movements against smuggling in "military education", saying a movement centred on "the pioneer, who thinks and works" cannot reach its goal "by adopting military methods of education and imitating Fascism".

unions-good.rationale: The 1918 Poale Zion outline calls the trade union movement "one of the most effective means in the present system for increasing the share of the workmen in the product", and the party builds Jewish unions in every country and in Palestine.

vanguard-party.rationale: Katznelson calls the pioneering labour movement the "vanguard" the masses need, yet warns that "professional revolutionaries ... impoverish the spirit of the movement".

war-builds-character.rationale: Katznelson says the World War "murdered our faith, poisoned our culture, wrecked our nerves" and created a militarist mentality that is "the foundation of the fascist movements".

women-suffrage.rationale: The Palestinian Poale Zion platform demands a "universal, equal, direct, and secret ballot" for all representative bodies, and the Achvah co-operatives rest on "universal suffrage without regard to sex".

worker-ownership.rationale: Poale Zion backs co-operatives and collective settlement, and Ben-Gurion ranks the kvutza above every other public body, but the 1918 outline calls co-operatives "mere attempts" not to be confused with Socialism and Ben-Gurion also welcomes private enterprise, so the sources point both ways.

workers-nation.rationale: Poale Zion organises Jewish workers on national lines in one world confederation yet joins "with workmen of every land" and the Socialist International, saying socialism is "international and not cosmopolitan".

workers-own-party.rationale: Poale Zion exists as a separate Jewish socialist labour party; in America it is "not affiliated either with the Socialist Party or with the Socialist Labor Party" and keeps "an independent attitude".

missingStatements.text: Settlers building a new society in their homeland should do the manual work themselves rather than rely on hired workers from the local population.
missingStatements.rationale: Katznelson and Ben-Gurion make Jewish labour a fundamental principle of settlement and defend the struggle for it.

missingStatements.text: A national fund should buy land that stays the permanent property of the nation, rather than land being sold to private owners.
missingStatements.rationale: Poale Zion describes the Jewish National Fund as land "to remain forever the property of the Jewish nation" and defends it against speculators.

missingStatements.text: Social change should be built now by pioneering co-operative communities that live the new society, rather than by waiting for a revolution.
missingStatements.rationale: Katznelson's revolutionary constructivism and the kvutza stress "a Socialist behavior here and now" and constructive achievement over destruction.

notes: Texts read in full or by topic: Borochov (National Question, Two Currents, Zion and Territory), the 1918 Poale Zion outline with its programmes, Syrkin's 1935 essays, Katznelson's Revolutionary Constructivism, Ben-Gurion's Rebirth and Destiny of Israel (keyword search of the whole book, Knesset speech on laws or a constitution read in full), Gordon via My Jewish Learning (no full text found), Divine's encyclopedia entry. Not found: Mapai and Ahdut HaAvoda platforms, the Histadrut constitution, Gordon's own essays, Borochov's Our Platform text. Judgement calls: Ben-Gurion's 1950 constitution speech is treated as the movement's position on courts and bills of rights because no strand states otherwise; the population-transfer statement is left null because Katznelson's remark about the Greek-Turkish exchange is one man's passing comment; where Borochovist and Hapoel Hatzair or Mapai strands differ on class struggle, materialism, strikes as a tool and collective farming the answer is 0 or low. The record fails or nearly fails the uncertainty rule on lines the movement did not write about (ecology, technology, gender, criminal justice).
